  uncertainty  +/- 0.07 epistemic (95% band 0.68-0.95); among patients I cannot tell apart the outcome was 0.69 of 1.00 mixed
  reliability  HIGH ('firm' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 88% of the time over the 33 labelled cases in this tier

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The EAU guidelines suggest that a PI-RADS threshold of $\ge 3$ is used to trigger a biopsy. The guideline states, "a PI-RADS threshold of $\ge 3$ is used to trigger biopsy [135, 226, 264, 375], at the cost of missing a small number of mainly ISUP GG 2 cancers, especially in biopsy-naive patients or in highly selected populations with high prevalence of csPCa (in which the MRI NPV decreases) [372, 472]."

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
EXPERT-STRUCTURED, your suggestion of biopsy is based on variables that the guideline makes decisive that no panel variable represents, such as the PI-RADS score. EXPERT-COHORT, the criterion confirms that the decision hinges on the PI-RADS score, which is a factor the guideline makes decisive, regardless of the prior-biopsy status or DRE findings.

WHAT THE DOCUMENTS MUST SETTLE
previous_notes - the prior biopsy status: at None the guideline does not dictate the action, but the cohort study suggests a threshold of $\ge 3$ would have avoided 30% of biopsies while missing 11% of ISUP GG $\ge 2$ cancer.
radiology_report - whether the lesion is compared against an earlier study: unchanged does not support re-sampling, new or larger does
psa_trend - the PSA trend: the guideline does not dictate the action based on the PSA trend alone.
laboratory_results - the laboratory results: the guideline does not dictate the action based on the laboratory results alone.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-PSA
interventions.who: Expert 2, PSA projector; the trajectory behind the headline PSA, with a conformal band
interventions.body:
Expert 2 here — the PSA projector. I read only the serial PSA the registrar opened.

TRAJECTORY: RISING (borderline). Last value 3.60 ng/mL over 3 points spanning 17 months; velocity +1.34 ng/mL per year; doubling time about 16 months.
PROJECTION at 6 months: 5.1 ng/mL, conformal 95% band 1.5-17.9.

Read the band before the point: it is wide by construction, and I only call a direction when the whole
band clears the last value. This does not vote on the biopsy — a rising PSA in a man with a known
diagnosis is the disease behaving as known — it tells the chair how fast the number is moving.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-FUSION
interventions.who: Expert 3, Extra-Trees on panel + laboratory + MRI prose; speaks only on documents that were opened
interventions.body:
Expert 3 here — the fusion classifier. I read the panel, the mpMRI report — the laboratory panel was not opened, so that block is imputed and my band is wider for it; nothing from the previous notes or the PSA series.

SUGGESTION: BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.80
  uncertainty  +/- 0.06 epistemic (95% band 0.69-0.91), of which 0.01 comes from values that had to be imputed
  reliability  HIGH ('firm' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 89% of the time over the 37 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, no prior biopsy, free PSA < 15%, DWI restriction in the report, lesion >= 15 mm in the report, suspicious DRE. Out-of-fold AUC 0.794. I am the only expert that has read the report's wording, and I still cannot see the prior grade or the
surveillance history: those are in the notes, and the registrar has to carry them.

data.gist: Expert 3 suggests BIOPSY, p=0.80 +/- 0.06, HIGH reliability (firm, fusion_nolab)

interventions.body:
SUFFICIENCY
The documents retrieved by the Registrar—radiology_report, psa_trend, and previous_notes—directly address all three moderator questions.

ALIGNMENT WITH THE PANEL
The retrieved evidence strongly aligns with the PANEL-PROTOCOL's answer of BIOPSY, as the PI-RADS 4 finding supports the cohort criterion, and the PSA trend shows a significant rise.

THE OPEN QUESTIONS, ONE BY ONE
Q1. The radiology_report states: "Focal PI-RADS 4 lesion in the left mid-gland peripheral zone."
Q2. The psa_trend indicates a rise from "1.7 (Aug 2023)" to "3.6 (Jan 2025)".
Q3. The previous_notes state the prior biopsy status was "None," and the surveillance protocol and planned management were not explicitly detailed beyond a referral for further assessment and imaging in May 2024.

WHAT CARRIES WEIGHT, AND WHY
The PI-RADS 4 finding is the most decisive variable as it directly triggers the cohort criterion, which the panel protocol confirms as the ruling factor. The rising PSA trend further supports the clinical concern.

MY SUGGESTION TO THE CHAIR
I suggest proceeding with a biopsy based on the PI-RADS 4 finding and the cohort criterion, as the retrieved evidence supports this path firmly.

VERDICT: ready | SUGGEST: biopsy | MISSING: none
